title: ChartBook snapshot
description: The record `chartbook snapshot` writes in the store: what one commit of a pipeline built. It has the index's envelope, with `code` and `made_at` in place of `generated_at` and `generator`. Its records are the index's asset records with fields left out, one for each asset the pipeline declares. The bytes are objects in the same store, under each record's `content_hash`. Version 2 (ChartBook 0.3) is kept as `_chartbook/snapshot.json` in the snapshot's own folder of its pipeline's folder in the store, and says for every file of every asset where the store keeps it (`stored`).

root.description: The ID of the pipeline the snapshot is of, as the pipeline named itself when it was made.

code.description: The code the assets were built from.

commit.description: The git commit the pipeline's repository was at, with nothing in the pipeline's folder uncommitted.

subdirectory.description: The pipeline's folder within its repository, with `/` between its parts. Absent for a pipeline at the top of its repository.

made_at.description: When the snapshot was made, in UTC. One commit can have several: a pipeline that pulls data from outside builds other bytes on another day. With the commit, this names the snapshot.

built_with.description: A note of the conditions the snapshot was made under. It is there to explain a difference between two snapshots, and no hash covers it. Nothing of the pipeline's .env is ever recorded.

run.description: True when ChartBook ran the pipeline's build in the same command that made the snapshot (`chartbook run --snapshot`). False when the snapshot took its owner's word that what was on disk was built by the commit.

chartbook.description: The version of ChartBook that made it.

python.description: The version of Python that ChartBook ran under.

platform.description: The operating system and machine type.

lineage.description: How the snapshot's lineage was checked when it was made: `pins` when its own pins were found to account for every dependency (every snapshot made since that check exists); `deep` when, with `chartbook snapshot --deep`, every snapshot upstream was walked and checked by hash as well. Missing on a snapshot made before either check. A note for audit; `chartbook lineage` checks again.

inputs.description: What the pipeline itself was pinned to when the snapshot was made: the `dependencies` of its own chartbook.lock, each with the commit and `pinned_hash` it was pinned at. Absent if it has no lockfile.

labels.description: The labels the pipeline's `[models.x.aliases]` gave when the snapshot was made, by the model's reference (`model/x`): each label and the first twelve or more hex digits of the version's content hash. `store gc` reads them from the newest snapshot, so a label given on one machine keeps its version on another; `chartbook pin` in a pipeline that depends on this one pins `this:model/x@label` from them. Absent if no label named a version.

index.description: The pipeline's own index at this commit, in the published form (no path of the machine that made it), as an object in the same store holding one `index.json`: what a docs build of the folder would have written just before the snapshot was made. It keeps the data dictionary of this version with its data. A model's versions in it are those made before this snapshot. Absent when the index could not be built (a manifest a docs build would refuse), and in snapshots made before snapshots carried it.

stored.description: Where the store keeps the asset's files: each file is kept once in its pipeline's folder, in the first snapshot that had it. `at` is where the asset is in the pipeline's folder (a file's folder, or the folder its files are listed from; empty for the top); `single` is true for an asset that is one file.

path.description: The file's path in the pipeline's folder, with `/` between parts.

kept_in.description: The snapshot's folder, in the same pipeline's folder, that keeps the file: this one, or an earlier one.

kept_as.description: The file's path in that folder, when it is not `path`: the same bytes kept under another name.

documents.description: The files a writer needs that are not assets, as one object in the same store, each under its path in the pipeline's folder: the manifest, the lockfile, the README, every `docs_path`, every file under the pipeline's `site_dir`, its logo and favicon; only files git tracks. Only plain paths inside the folder, none a link or under one. With the assets, enough to lay the version out as a folder and build its site from the store alone. Absent when git tracks none of them, and in snapshots made before snapshots carried them.

files.description: The documents' paths in the pipeline's folder, with `/`, sorted.

stored.description: Where the store keeps the asset's files: each file is kept once in its pipeline's folder, in the first snapshot that had it. `at` is where the asset is in the pipeline's folder (a file's folder, or the folder its files are listed from; empty for the top); `single` is true for an asset that is one file.

path.description: The file's path in the pipeline's folder, with `/` between parts.

kept_in.description: The snapshot's folder, in the same pipeline's folder, that keeps the file: this one, or an earlier one.

kept_as.description: The file's path in that folder, when it is not `path`: the same bytes kept under another name.

records.description: One record per asset the pipeline declares with a `path`, and per dataframe that is a table or a query in a source (written out as `<name>.parquet` into the store when the source is a DuckDB file; its `location` is the source's), sorted by the asset's reference. One with a `content_hash` was built; one without was declared and not built when the snapshot was made.

keep.description: The manifest marks the asset `keep = true`: every version of its bytes is kept in the store, each in the newest snapshot holding it, by `store gc`. Present only when it does.

stored.description: Where the store keeps the asset's files: each file is kept once in its pipeline's folder, in the first snapshot that had it. `at` is where the asset is in the pipeline's folder (a file's folder, or the folder its files are listed from; empty for the top); `single` is true for an asset that is one file.

path.description: The file's path in the pipeline's folder, with `/` between parts.

kept_in.description: The snapshot's folder, in the same pipeline's folder, that keeps the file: this one, or an earlier one.

kept_as.description: The file's path in that folder, when it is not `path`: the same bytes kept under another name.

tags.description: The git tags on the snapshot's commit when it was made: the names of that version. A tag made later is not in it.

repository.description: The repository the snapshot was made in: the web address of its `origin` remote, with no credentials. A dependency named by its ID alone keeps to the repository it was first pinned from.

first_commit.description: The first commit of the repository the snapshot was made in, back from its commit by first parents: the same in every full clone, with a remote or none. Absent for a shallow clone. With `repository`, it tells one repository from another that gives itself the same pipeline ID.

made_by.description: Who made it: `snapshot` (the default) for one its pipeline's owner made; `pin` for one a pin made from a clone of the pipeline's repository, which a pin by ID never chooses.
